data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Flux batch script
#
# NOTE: This script uses Snakemake's DRMAA integration with LSF-style arguments.
# Flux does not provide a DRMAA interface by default, so this functionality cannot be translated directly.
#
# Performance implication of omission: without a Flux-targeting executor, Snakemake will not be able to
# submit rules as separate scheduled jobs (reduced parallelism/throughput), unless you adapt it to a Flux
# executor/plugin supported at your site.

# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./netseq.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with default resources (no explicit LSF CPU/mem/time were specified).

JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  set -o nounset -o pipefail -o errexit -x

  module load fastqc
  module load bowtie2
  module load samtools
  module load subread
  module load gcc/7.4.0
  module load R/4.0.3

  mkdir -p logs

  run_snakemake() {
      local snake_file=$1
      local config_file=$2

      args='\
          -oo {log.out} \
          -eo {log.err} \
          -J {params.job_name}\
          -R "rusage[mem={params.memory}] span[hosts=1]"\
          -n {threads} '

      snakemake -n \
          --snakefile "$snake_file" \
          --drmaa "$args" \
          --jobs 100 \
          --configfiles $config_file
  }

  pipe_dir=src/pipelines
  samples=SAMPLES.yaml

  snake=$pipe_dir/NETseq.snake
  config=NETseq.yaml
  flux run -n 1 bash -lc "run_snakemake '$snake' '$samples $config'"

  snake=$pipe_dir/pauses.snake
  config=pauses.yaml
  flux run -n 1 bash -lc "run_snakemake '$snake' '$samples $config'"
fi
"
}

No explicit CPU core count (`-c`) or time limit (`-t`) is requested; the job will run with Flux defaults, which may be insufficient for `--jobs 100` and can limit throughput (resource sizing concern).
